program if_then

      implicit none

      integer                   ::      num1
      integer, parameter        ::      num2 = 5

      print *, "Enter a number between 1 and 10 -> "
      read *, num1

      if (num1 > num2) then
              print *, "Number entered greater than 5!"
      end if

end program if_then
, so it is a compile-time constant. It never gets a stack slot.
keeps each instruction on one line. Each instruction line is the address, the machine bytes, and the Intel disassembly. The notes after

opens a 0x220-byte frame because each Fortran I/O statement builds a unit descriptor on the stack. The descriptor fields in the listing are internal to libgfortran. The calls around them are the part that matches the source.
The prompt is written in three calls.
The read is the same shape with the read entry points.
